platform-maintenance.title: Platform maintenance: upstream activity becomes integration work

ideas.title: Kubernetes as a shared substrate, not a universal application requirement
ideas.summary: Kubernetes won a durable infrastructure role; application suitability still depends on isolation, scale and operational capacity.

ideas.title: Elastic scheduling with explicit disruption and resource budgets
ideas.summary: Autoscaling matured into useful capacity control, but cost optimization cannot ignore workload disruption.

ideas.title: Operators and virtual tenancy as platform software
ideas.summary: Controllers and virtual control planes improve reuse but create software and security responsibilities of their own.

ideas.title: GitOps reconciliation and auditable desired state
ideas.summary: GitOps succeeded as a repeatable reconciliation pattern; it did not settle every deployment or business-model problem.

ideas.title: Progressive release requires trustworthy feedback
ideas.summary: Canaries and feature flags can limit exposure, but automation is only as reliable as its health signals and rollback boundaries.

ideas.title: CI pipelines as production trust boundaries
ideas.summary: Centralized CI improved repeatability while concentrating credentials and third-party execution risk.

ideas.title: Internal platforms as products with measurable users
ideas.summary: Platform engineering works best as a service to developers with feedback, ownership and a narrow initial scope.

ideas.title: Developer portals are interfaces, not the whole platform
ideas.summary: Catalogs and templates help discovery, but a portal cannot substitute for functioning delivery and ownership systems.

ideas.title: Delivery and developer-experience metrics without ranking theater
ideas.summary: Measurement is useful for local improvement and becomes misleading when activity is treated as individual value.

ideas.title: Infrastructure as code and the cost of governance changes
ideas.summary: Declarative infrastructure remained durable, while licensing changes made governance and exit planning part of architecture.

ideas.title: General-purpose languages do not guarantee infrastructure product fit
ideas.summary: Language ergonomics are useful, but a programming-language wrapper alone does not establish a sustainable infrastructure tool.

ideas.title: Composable control planes for internal APIs
ideas.summary: Crossplane-style composition can make infrastructure self-service, but the platform team still owns API design and lifecycle behavior.

ideas.title: eBPF as an infrastructure implementation technique
ideas.summary: eBPF gained a durable role in networking and visibility, while operational responsibility moved into a different layer.

ideas.title: Service mesh simplification through ambient architecture
ideas.summary: Ambient mesh reduces per-workload proxy coupling but does not remove identity, policy and traffic-management complexity.

ideas.title: Gateway modernization and the failure of assumed maintenance
ideas.summary: Widely deployed infrastructure still needs funded maintainers, migration paths and explicit lifecycle ownership.

ideas.title: Open instrumentation and portable telemetry interfaces
ideas.summary: OpenTelemetry became a durable instrumentation standard; backend and operational portability remain incomplete.

ideas.title: Telemetry budgets, cardinality and sampling
ideas.summary: Collecting everything is not a sustainable observability strategy; selective data needs explicit diagnostic tradeoffs.

ideas.title: Outcome-driven signals instead of dashboard accumulation
ideas.summary: Observability helps when it closes a diagnostic or response loop; more dashboards do not establish reliability.

ideas.title: Recovery engineering beyond having backups
ideas.summary: Recovery readiness means restoring the required scope within a useful time, not merely possessing backup data.

ideas.title: Resilience follows dependencies, not region labels
ideas.summary: Multiple regions or providers improve resilience only when the critical dependencies and recovery paths are genuinely independent.

ideas.title: SLOs, incident learning and bounded experiments
ideas.summary: Reliability practices work when they change operational decisions and recovery behavior, rather than merely produce reports.

ideas.title: Artifact provenance and signing as verifiable evidence
ideas.summary: Signing and build provenance matured into useful trust evidence, but neither proves that software is benign.

ideas.title: SBOMs are inventory inputs, not a remediation outcome
ideas.summary: Software inventories help exposure analysis, but actionable security requires context, ownership and a reliable remediation loop.

ideas.title: Defense beyond shift-left and dependency scanning
ideas.summary: Early checks are valuable, but build compromise and malicious maintenance require controls across the software lifecycle.

ideas.title: FinOps and cost per useful outcome
ideas.summary: Cloud cost management matured when engineering decisions were tied to useful output, ownership and financial accountability.

ideas.title: Selective cloud repatriation and simpler deployment
ideas.summary: Repatriation can fit stable workloads and capable teams; a successful exit is not a general case against public cloud.

ideas.title: Portable cost data versus portable workloads
ideas.summary: FOCUS improves the interface for cost analysis, while workload exit and multi-cloud operations remain separate engineering problems.

ideas.title: Right-sized services and modular simplicity
ideas.summary: Service decomposition is valuable when boundaries justify it; simpler deployment can win when coordination and operations dominate.

ideas.title: Serverless and managed containers as selective operating models
ideas.summary: Managed execution expanded its workload range, while cold starts, limits and provider coupling remained design inputs.

ideas.title: Hermetic builds and shared caches
ideas.summary: Reproducibility and reusable build work are durable engineering ideas, but their value depends on explicit inputs and trustworthy caches.

ideas.title: Development containers and remote environments
ideas.summary: Repeatable environments can reduce setup friction, while remote execution introduces cost, access and provider-lifecycle tradeoffs.

ideas.title: Cloud workspace product resets and AI repositioning
ideas.summary: Cloud development infrastructure remained useful while particular deployment and product strategies were replaced.

ideas.title: AI assistance with measured accepted outcomes
ideas.summary: AI assistance can change engineering work, but adoption and perceived speed are not sufficient productivity evidence.

ideas.title: Incident agents with bounded authority and reproducible evaluations
ideas.summary: AI diagnosis is promising, but the reviewed evidence does not establish reliable unattended remediation across production environments.

ideas.title: Inference operations are still capacity, reliability and cost engineering
ideas.summary: AI serving creates new workload characteristics but still depends on explicit scheduling, service objectives and unit economics.

ideas.title: Short-lived workload identity and CI federation
ideas.summary: Workload identity reduces dependence on distributed long-lived credentials while making identity policy an essential operating service.

ideas.title: Admission policy and runtime detection as complementary controls
ideas.summary: Policy enforcement and runtime detection matured, but effective response still requires maintained rules and operational ownership.

ideas.title: Hardware choice and interruption-aware capacity
ideas.summary: ARM and interruptible capacity are useful optimization options, but headline price-performance claims require workload-level validation.

ideas.title: Carbon-aware operations and honest measurement boundaries
ideas.summary: Carbon-aware scheduling has a coherent measurement framework, but evidence of broad realized operational benefit remains limited here.

ideas.title: Durable execution for long-running coordination
ideas.summary: Durable workflow engines provide a useful alternative to custom retry and orchestration code when their programming model fits.

ideas.title: WebAssembly as a specialized execution boundary
ideas.summary: WebAssembly supports a credible specialized execution ecosystem, but the evidence here does not establish replacement of general container platforms.

ideas.title: Stateful elasticity needs resumable application-aware control
ideas.summary: Stateful scaling is useful when data movement, placement and overlapping requests form a recoverable lifecycle.

ideas.title: Migration-safe infrastructure refactoring
ideas.summary: Code reuse is most useful when resource identity and traffic movement remain explicit during a migration.

ideas.title: Locality-aware routing must account for cache and backend costs
ideas.summary: A local network hop can be cheaper while the full request becomes more expensive.

extension.purpose: Add incident-assistance, agent-network, policy-enforcement and platform-maintenance evidence; refine authority and outcome distinctions.
